01Start hereSet up your first licenseStart with your identity, a license and its expiration date. You can return to the other setup steps later.+

A signed-in account with active Credential access. NPI lookup needs a connection.

Watch the walkthrough

0:50 · Narrated demo with captions. Synthetic data; no live messages or payments.

Read the transcript
First license Demonstration records only. No real messages, payments or AI requests occur. Start in Setup under More. Check your name, degree and primary state. Add a license, then use the expiration date on your current document. If you use an NPI match, review it before importing. Your saved record and its supporting document are separate steps. You can return to Setup later. Demo license. A saved record is not board verification.

Download transcriptDownload video

  1. Open More, then Setup. Open About you and check your name, degree and primary state.
  2. Open Your licenses. Review any NPI lookup match before importing it, or add the license yourself.
  3. Open Expiration dates and enter the date shown on your current license. A public registry match may not include that date.
  4. Open Credentials, then Licenses to check the saved record. Return to Setup when you are ready to add its document or another credential.

Good to know

  • A saved record is different from attached proof. Setup tracks both.
  • Setup can be resumed. A completed setup step does not verify that a license is active with its board.
  • Compare the plans here, then create your account. Founding Credential is $99/year for the first 100 paid founding members. Availability is confirmed before payment; creating an account does not reserve a place. Paid membership requires a card at checkout and your explicit agreement.
  • After the 100 paid founding memberships, early-bird Credential is $149/year, followed by standard Credential at $199/year.

You’re done when: The correct license and expiration date appear in your records.

02Start hereUpload and review a licenseSmart Scan prepares a record from your document. Check the extracted details before saving.+

A connection and available AI access. Shared access has usage limits; an optional own key can be set in Settings.

Watch the walkthrough

0:50 · Narrated demo with captions. Synthetic data; no live messages or payments.

Read the transcript
Scan a license Demonstration records only. No real messages, payments or AI requests occur. Add on your phone and Documents on your desktop open Smart Scan. Upload the license and wait for its review card. Check the type, number, state and dates against the original; fix anything that is wrong before saving. If analysis fails, check Documents first. The file may already be saved, ready to file when AI access is available. Demo analysis result. Real Smart Scan uploads are sent to AI.

Download transcriptDownload video

  1. On a phone, tap Add. On a desktop, open Documents. Both open Smart Scan.
  2. Choose Upload for a file or Camera for a photo. Use the credential itself and keep the text readable.
  3. In the review card, check the document type, License #, State, Issued and Expires against the original. Correct any mistakes.
  4. Choose Save to License. Open Credentials, then Licenses and check the saved record and attached document.

Good to know

  • Scanning sends the supplied content to the AI provider. Keep patient records out of credential uploads.
  • If analysis fails, read the error first: the document may already be saved. Find it in Documents and use File with AI when available, or add the record manually; avoid repeatedly uploading the same file.

You’re done when: The reviewed license record is linked to its document.

Smart Scan requires a connection and available AI access. Manual CME entry is also available.

CME certificate Demonstration records only. No real messages, payments or AI requests occur. Upload your CME certificate, then review it as a CME Credit. Match the completion date, hours, category and provider to the certificate. Add topics that reflect the actual course. Save, then check the entry in CME Credits. A topic tag helps the calculator organize hours; it does not prove that a board accepts this course. Demo certificate. Review AI output; course acceptance is not verified.

Download transcriptDownload video

  1. Open Add on a phone or Documents on a desktop, then Upload the certificate.
  2. Check that the review card is a CME Credit. Compare the title, completion date, hours, credit category and provider with the certificate.
  3. Review the topic tags against the course content. Choose Save to CME Credit.

Good to know

  • A topic tag helps the tracker count an entry. It does not prove that a board accepts the course.

04Credentials & CMEImport a CME transcriptReview a batch of credits before adding it, including duplicates and missing fields.+

PDF, CSV or XLSX file, or pasted text. Other PDF layouts may need available AI access.

Watch the walkthrough

1:00 · Narrated demo with captions. Synthetic data; no live messages or payments.

Read the transcript
Transcript import Demonstration records only. No real messages, payments or AI requests occur. Import a transcript from CME Credits. Choose a supported file or paste text. If prompted, match the columns, then review the selected rows. Duplicates begin unticked. Check dates, hours and credit types and correct missing fields. Nothing enters the log until you add the batch. Afterward, link individual certificates from Documents if you need them. Demo import. No direct CE Broker or ACCME account connection.

Download transcriptDownload video

Open this video guide on its own page

  1. Open Credentials, then CME Credits and choose Import transcript.
  2. Choose transcript file (PDF, CSV, XLSX), or select Paste text instead. Which formats, which columns? explains the available layouts.
  3. If asked, map the columns and choose Continue to review. Check every included row's title, date, hours and credit type.
  4. Leave duplicates unticked unless you have checked that they are separate activities. Fix missing fields and review topic tags.
  5. Choose Add to CME log when the selection is correct. Check the confirmation and the entries in CME Credits.

Good to know

  • The Add button includes the selected row count and hours. Nothing is added to the CME log until you choose it.
  • Imported transcript rows do not automatically supply individual certificates. Link those from Documents when needed.
  • A known layout describes the parser, not a verification that the credits qualify. Some other PDF layouts are sent to AI; review the import screen's explanation.

You’re done when: The intended activities appear once, with the right fields and total hours.

05Credentials & CMEUnderstand your CME calculationCheck the counted dates, credit categories and rule source before deciding what to do next.+

Your saved license and CME records. Opening board sources or sending a rule report needs a connection.

Watch the walkthrough

1:00 · Narrated demo with captions. Synthetic data; no live messages or payments.

Read the transcript
Understand a CME calculation Demonstration records only. No real messages, payments or AI requests occur. Open Compliance and start with the dates being counted. A credit may be outside this renewal or have the wrong category. Read the rule's source and review date. If the app asks whether a condition applies, keep Not sure until you can confirm. Use Rules changed? to report a specific discrepancy. The calculation organizes your records; it does not approve your renewal. Record organization only. The app does not approve a renewal.

Download transcriptDownload video

Open this video guide on its own page

  1. Open Credentials, then CME Credits and choose Compliance.
  2. Find the state you are reviewing. Read the dates used for its calculation and check them against the license you are renewing.
  3. Check total hours, category minimums and topic rows. Review entries outside the cycle or missing a category before adding more credit.
  4. Open the source link and read its review date. If an applicability question appears, answer for that license; keep Not sure until you can confirm.
  5. Use Rules changed? to report a specific discrepancy with a board link and explanation. Confirm unclear requirements with the board.

Good to know

  • The tracker uses your saved records and rules on file. A completed bar is not a board decision or a guarantee of compliance.
  • The Ohio pain-clinic question is an explicit conditional-rule pilot. Other exceptions may be described in notes without being fully calculated.
  • The app does not submit your license renewal.

You’re done when: You understand which records were counted and which requirements or conditions still need confirmation.

06Locum work & paymentsSet up a locum agreementSave the terms that your work log and invoices will use.+

New paid Credential members receive a separate 30-day Practice trial when their first annual payment is confirmed. It ends without an added charge. Continuing Practice requires an explicit purchase. Existing Credential members should contact support@credentialdomd.com to review options for adding Practice; no change or charge will occur without their agreement. The paid Credential membership continues, and existing Practice records remain available to read and export. Eligible people who signed up under the earlier free-beta wording receive 30 days free with no card, starting when they first activate their account with a verified email address. The app shows the exact end date; signing in again does not restart those 30 days. You may opt in to $99/year Credential during the beta by adding a card and explicitly agreeing to the annual subscription. Your first charge is scheduled for your original beta end date, when your paid year starts. Choosing early does not charge you early or start a new trial. You keep the same account and saved records. If you never opt in, there is no automatic charge and nothing to cancel. Paid membership renews annually unless canceled. Existing accounts eligible under the announced lifetime-access policy keep Credential and Practice free for life. A waitlist entry alone does not qualify for lifetime access. Account eligibility must be confirmed before asking an existing member to pay.

Agreement to reviewed rates Demonstration records only. No real messages, payments or AI requests occur. Open Practice, then Contracts. The Agreements screen holds the terms used for billing. Add the facility, recipient and dates, then the rate types your agreement actually uses. Check the billing increment, any stipend coverage and overage terms. These fields drive your invoices, so compare them with the agreement before using them. Select the reviewed agreement in Work. Illustrative agreement and rates; not market-rate advice.

Download transcriptDownload video

  1. Open Practice, then Contracts. Choose Add to open Add Agreement.
  2. Enter Hospital / Facility, Agency (if any), Invoice recipient email and the agreement's dates.
  3. Enter the rates that apply: hourly work, a day rate, call stipend, hours included in a stipend, overage or orientation. Check the billing increment too.
  4. Compare every amount and date with your agreement before saving. If you used Smart Scan to extract a contract, review its fields before Save to Contract.
  5. Open Work and select this agreement before logging time.

Good to know

  • Only enter rate types that apply to your agreement. Missing or incorrect rates can produce an incorrect invoice.
  • The app records the terms you provide. It does not resolve contract disputes.

You’re done when: The correct agreement is available in Work with reviewed rates.

Log past work Demonstration records only. No real messages, payments or AI requests occur. Choose the agreement before logging work. Use Log past time, then check the date, type and times. A billing note goes on the invoice, so leave patient information out. Save with Log it and compare logged time, billed time and amount. Rounding and stipend terms come from your agreement. Demo time entry. Keep patient information out of billing notes.

Download transcriptDownload video

  1. Open Practice, then Work and select the agreement for this work.
  2. Choose Log past time. Check the date, work type, start and end times and selected agreement.
  3. Add a short Billing note only if you want that text on the invoice. Keep patient details out of billing notes.
  4. Choose Log it. Check the saved entry's logged time, billed time and amount before invoicing.

Good to know

  • The agreement's increment and stipend terms can make billed time differ from elapsed time.

You’re done when: The work entry belongs to the intended agreement and shows the expected billed amount.

09Locum work & paymentsRecord a full or partial paymentKeep the remaining balance accurate as payments arrive.+

An existing invoice in Practice.

Watch the walkthrough

1:00 · Narrated demo with captions. Synthetic data; no live messages or payments.

Read the transcript
Partial then full payment Demonstration records only. No real messages, payments or AI requests occur. When money arrives, find the invoice and record the amount and date received. A partial payment leaves the remaining balance open. Record the next installment when it arrives. This is your payment ledger; payments are entered by you, not imported automatically from a bank. Writing off a balance is different from receiving money. Demo ledger entries. No money moves and no bank is connected.

Download transcriptDownload video

  1. Open Practice, then Invoices and find the invoice that was paid.
  2. Choose Record payment. Enter Amount received and Date received from the payment you actually received.
  3. Optionally add a check or remittance reference. Check the amount against the open balance.
  4. Choose Record partial payment or Record — settles the invoice, as shown for the amount you entered.
  5. Open the invoice and check Payments received and Still owed. Record another payment when the next installment arrives.

Good to know

  • You record payments yourself; the app does not pull them from your bank or agency.
  • Write off remaining balance closes the balance without recording money received. Use it only when that is the action you intend.

You’re done when: The recorded payments and remaining balance match your records.

Reminder expectations Demonstration records only. No real messages, payments or AI requests occur. Check your email and reminder settings. Email expiration digests depend on the service's scheduled check and mail delivery. Browser alerts need permission and an open app on this device.   1. Open More, then Settings. Check the email in your profile and the reminder settings.
  2. Set a lead time and frequency. Enable Email reminders if you want expiration digests for the records covered by the service.
  3. Enable browser notifications and grant permission if you want alerts on this device. The browser alert check runs while the app is open.

Good to know

  • A setting or browser permission is not confirmation that an email arrived.

11Help & accountFollow a support ticketKeep the problem, follow-up details and replies together in one place.+

A signed-in account and a connection. If you cannot sign in, email support@credentialdomd.com.

Watch the walkthrough

0:50 · Narrated demo with captions. Synthetic data; no live messages or payments.

Read the transcript
Follow your ticket Demonstration records only. No real messages, payments or AI requests occur. Tell support the screen, what you tried and what happened. Include the exact error if there is one. Keep private information out of screenshots. After submitting, check Your tickets for the conversation, even if email has not arrived. Add updates to the same ticket. Support may use AI assistance; ask for human review if needed. Mark it resolved when the issue is solved. Demo thread and simulated replies. No support message is sent.

Download transcriptDownload video

  1. Open Get help in the app. Describe the screen, what you tried, what you expected and the exact error if one appeared.
  2. Add a screenshot only if it helps. Remove patient details, passwords, keys and unrelated personal information first.
  3. After submitting, open Your tickets and select the ticket to see its status and replies.
  4. If it still has No replies yet, add useful details with Add to this ticket and Send reply. Check this thread even if an email has not arrived.
  5. When the problem is solved, choose Mark as resolved.

Good to know

  • Submission confirms that the ticket was filed, not that the problem has been fixed.
  • Support replies are shown in the ticket and can also be emailed. No guaranteed response time is advertised here.
  • Support may use AI assistance. Ask for a human review when the answer does not resolve your question.
  • No-hassle 100% money-back guarantee: request a full refund of your most recent annual membership payment, including a renewal payment, at any time. There is no request deadline or prorating. This covers your most recent annual payment, not all payments from past years. Request through Get help in the app or support@credentialdomd.com. You do not need to delete your account, saved records or reports to request a refund.

You’re done when: You can find the original ticket, read its replies and continue the same conversation.

12Help & accountBack up records and private notesKeep a copy you control and understand what stays in this browser.+

Your loaded records in this browser. Cloud files that have not downloaded may not be available offline.

Watch the walkthrough

0:50 · Narrated demo with captions. Synthetic data; no live messages or payments.

Read the transcript
Backup and device move Demonstration records only. No real messages, payments or AI requests occur. Export a copy from Data & Backup. Private work notes stay in this browser, so export those when moving devices. These files contain readable data; the app does not encrypt them. Sign in on the new device for synced records and restore your notes file. Check the result before clearing the old browser or signing out. Demo files only. Readable backups must be kept private.

Download transcriptDownload video

  1. Open More, then Data & Backup. Choose Export JSON Backup to save a copy of your loaded data.
  2. If you use private work notes, check the Private notes count on this device. Export to a file makes a separate copy of those notes.
  3. Store these files somewhere you control. They contain readable data and are not encrypted by the app.
  4. On a new device, sign in to load synced records. Export any current data before Restore from Backup: a JSON restore can replace the collections in the file and update settings. For a notes-only export, use Restore from a file in Private notes.
  5. Check the restored records and notes before clearing data on the old device.

Good to know

  • Private notes do not sync automatically and are not included in the server's monthly backup. A manual JSON export can include them.
  • Signing out or clearing browser storage can remove local notes. The app does not encrypt its private-note storage.
  • Keep both the original backup and an export of current data until you have checked the restored records and notes.

You’re done when: You have a saved export and know which notes need a manual transfer.

13SharingChoose and share a reference draftAsk Vera for a draft, choose the saved contacts to include, and review the text before sharing.+

Saved peer references and access to Vera. Preparing a draft through Vera requires available AI access; contact details are assembled locally for the displayed draft.

Watch the walkthrough

0:55 · Narrated demo with captions. Synthetic data; no live messages or payments.

Read the transcript
Share selected references Demonstration records only. No real messages, payments or AI requests occur. Ask Vera to prepare a draft from your saved peer references. In the reference draft, choose who to include. Remove anyone who should not be in this request, then check the remaining names and contact details. Copy draft prepares text for you to paste. Open in email opens your mail app. Neither choice sends the message for you. Review the recipient before completing delivery. Demo contacts. Copy draft and Open in email do not send a message.

Download transcriptDownload video

  1. Ask Vera to prepare a draft from your saved peer references.
  2. In the reference draft, choose who to include. Uncheck anyone you want excluded and review the remaining names and contact details.
  3. Choose Copy draft to copy the reviewed text, or Open in email to prepare a message in your email app.
  4. Check the recipient and the complete message before you send it.

Good to know

  • The reference draft is shown in Vera. Peer References has a separate Select and share flow.
  • Copying a draft or opening an email does not send it. Tutorial demonstrations use synthetic contacts and simulate sharing.
  • If a selected record is no longer available, prepare a fresh draft before sharing.

You’re done when: The intended contacts remain in the reviewed draft, with excluded contacts left out.
